To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the online information literacy learning object sample from PRIMO is generally weak in its use of best practices for teaching critical thinking.

the majority of PRIMO online information literacy learning object do not encourage or assess critical thinking, and that those that do are not necessarily following best practices for teaching or assessing critical thinking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: To what extent and in what ways do information literacy online learning object follow best practices for assessing and teaching critical thinking?
how the critical thinking skills and dispositions can be taught and assessed through information literacy online instruction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
information literacy online learning object creators follow best practices in teaching critical thinking to some extent.
information literacy online learning object authors do not follow best practices for critical thinking in a consistent or systematic manner.
information literacy online learning object creators follow best practices for assessing and teaching critical thinking to some extent and to varying degrees, and there is much room for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information literacy online learning object sample is not following best practices for teaching or assessing critical thinking.

this study has demonstrated that information literacy online learning object authors do not follow best practices for assessing critical thinking, but do follow best practices for encouraging critical thinking to a limited extent.
we have developed an instrument for assessing critical thinking in information literacy online learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information literacy instruction is not always explicitly designed to promote critical thinking, and when critical thinking is encouraged, it is not always assessed.
information literacy online learning object authors are not currently following best practices for teaching critical thinking.

information literacy learning objects can be designed to teach and assess critical thinking, and that the ACRL Information Literacy Competency Standards for Higher Education provide a framework for doing so.
